title: RNA Extraction and RT-PCR on Mouse Tissues
author: Jayshen Arudkumar
materials: Keep the tissue samples on ice

The New England Biolabs (NEB) website can be consulted for the finer details of reaction volumes and components when amplifying using a standard NEB Taq DNA Polymerase and the 10X Standard Taq Reaction Buffer. The primers we used are listed in Supplementary Figure S2. We recommend using cDNA synthesised from 1-2 μg of RNA, as well as assembling all rection components on ice prior to transferring to the preheated thermocycler. After the RT-PCR, confirm the expected band sizes by carefully visualizing the amplified products on a 1% agarose gel.

steps.title: Prepare Centrifuge
steps.instruction: Set the centrifuge to cool at 4°C.

steps.title: Tissue Homogenization
steps.instruction: Mince heart and skeletal muscle tissues in a few drops of water and homogenize using a bead-based system.

substeps.instruction: Place minced portions into a magNA lyser tube.
Homogenize in the Precellys bead-based homogeniser at 6500 RPM for 2 cycles of 20s each.

steps.title: RNA Phase Separation
steps.instruction: Extract RNA using TRIzol and chloroform.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 μL of Invitrogen TRIzol reagent to the supernatant.
Incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature (RT) to dissociate the nucleoprotein complex.
Add 100 μL chloroform (ratio of 0.2 ml chloroform per 1 ml TRIZOL reagent).
Shake tubes vigorously by hand for 15 seconds to mix.
Incubate for 2 min at RT.
Centrifuge at 12,000 RCF in a 4°C cooled centrifuge for 15 minutes.

steps.title: RNA Precipitation and Column Loading
steps.instruction: Isolate the aqueous phase and prepare for spin column purification.

substeps.instruction: Label new microcentrifuge tubes and keep on ice.
Transfer approximately 175 μL of the colourless liquid layer to a new eppendorf tube.
Add an equal volume of 70% ethanol.
Mix by pipetting and invert the tube to disperse any visible precipitate.
Transfer a maximum of 700 μL to the QIAGEN spin column with a collection tube.
Centrifuge for 30 seconds at 8,000 RCF (room temperature centrifuge).

steps.title: RNA Column Washing
steps.instruction: Wash the spin column to remove contaminants.

substeps.instruction: Place the flow-through back into the spin column and centrifuge again for 30 seconds at 6,500 RCF.
Discard the flow-through and place the column back into the collection tube.
Add 700 μL Buffer RW1 to the RNeasy spin column and centrifuge for 15 seconds at 8,000 RCF.
Add 500 μL Buffer RPE to the RNeasy spin column and centrifuge for 15 seconds at 8,000 RCF.
Discard the flow-through and place the spin column in a new collection tube.
Add 500 μL Buffer RPE to the RNeasy spin column and centrifuge for 2 minutes at 8,000 RCF.

steps.title: RNA Elution
steps.instruction: Dry the membrane and elute the purified RNA.

substeps.instruction: Discard the flow-through and place the spin column in a new collection tube.
Centrifuge for 1 minute at max speed.
Place the RNeasy spin column in a new QIAGEN RNase-free 1.5 ml tube.
Add 30-50 μL RNase-free water directly to the spin column membrane.
Centrifuge for 1 minute at 8,000 RCF to elute the RNA (for 100 μg, use 2–3 sequential 100 μL elutions).

steps.title: RNA Quality Control
steps.instruction: Measure the concentration and purity of the RNA solution using a NanoDrop Spectrophotometer.

substeps.instruction: Verify that the A260/A280 ratio is approximately 2.0 (acceptable range: 1.8 to 2.1).

steps.title: cDNA Synthesis
steps.instruction: Convert RNA to cDNA and prepare for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Follow the High-Capacity cDNA Reverse Transcription Kit (Applied Biosystems) protocol to convert 1-2 μg of RNA into cDNA.
Dilute cDNA in 50 μL ultrapure water prior to running downstream analysis.
